idiom_name: test-helper translation unit of struct factory functions (designated initializers for the base)
implementation_notes: C has neither classes nor a test-fixture mechanism, so the mother becomes a plain test-helper translation unit: customer_mother.h declares functions such as 'struct customer customer_vip(void)' - or out-parameter fillers when the graph is large - that return fully initialised structs. C99 designated initializers already make a single struct literal self-documenting, so reserve the mother for multi-struct graphs and for centralising invariant-bearing defaults (valid ids, tiers, dates), and extend the literal at the call site for one-off variation instead of adding another mother function. Where the graph owns heap memory, pair each factory with a '*_free' counterpart or keep it in fixed-size storage so tests do not leak or double-free.
pitfalls: Returning a struct that holds owning pointers copies the pointers: two calls to the mother hand out the same buffers unless the factory deep-copies or the caller takes ownership explicitly.
A static counter inside the mother (for unique ids) makes outcomes depend on execution order and breaks test isolation; pass ids in or reset state per test.
String literals stored in 'char *' members are immutable in practice; declare them 'const char *' or copy into the struct's own buffer.
Nothing links the mother into the build automatically: it must be added to the test target, and header-only functions need 'static inline' to avoid duplicate symbols across translation units.
